subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Fuel Injection Takes Over
description: One-minute skill: Fuel Injection Takes Over.

hook.text: Electronic fuel injection replaced the carburetor by metering fuel with computer precision.

buildup.text: Sensors measure airflow, temperature, and throttle position dozens of times per second.

discovery.text: The computer calculates exact fuel needs and commands injectors to spray into the intake.

twist.text: Fuel injection improved power, efficiency, and cold starts so dramatically that carburetors vanished.

climax.text: The switch to injection cut emissions enough to meet strict clean-air laws of the 1980s.

punchline.text: A computer replaced a century of mechanical guesswork.

quiz.question: What was a key advantage of fuel injection over carburetors?

details.summary: Electronic fuel injection replaced carburetors throughout the 1980s and 1990s, using sensors and computers to precisely meter fuel delivery, dramatically improving emissions, efficiency, cold starting, and reliability.
details.whyItMatters: Fuel injection was the most significant engine technology shift of the late 20th century. It made catalytic converters effective, enabled tighter emissions standards, and made engines reliably self-adjusting.
takeaways: Electronic sensors measure airflow, temperature, and exhaust composition
Computers calculate exact fuel requirements thousands of times per second
Carburetors were effectively obsolete by the mid-1990s

faq.question: Why was fuel injection better than carburetors?
faq.answer: Carburetors used mechanical means to mix fuel and air, which was imprecise and sensitive to altitude and temperature. Fuel injection measures conditions electronically and adjusts in milliseconds for optimal combustion.

faq.question: When did carburetors completely disappear from new cars?
faq.answer: The last new car sold with a carburetor in the US was the 1990 Subaru Justy. By the mid-1990s, virtually all new cars worldwide used fuel injection to meet increasingly strict emissions regulations.
